# Polyfills on SingleStore

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_polyfill_docs.py from provisa/transpiler/polyfill: do not edit by hand. -->

A polyfill is how Provisa gives a PostgreSQL client PostgreSQL's behaviour on SingleStore (dialect `singlestore`), as a serving engine or as a source a statement is sent to directly. Each feature has a read polyfill, how its values and operations are computed there, and a write polyfill, how its values reach it; each states its limitations.

This page lists every feature that has a polyfill or a limitation on SingleStore. A feature SingleStore does natively with no difference from PostgreSQL is left out and counted. The conformance runs check the omission: a feature left out that answers otherwise than PostgreSQL fails the run.

When SingleStore is a serving engine reading a source it attaches directly, it may push work into that source, with the source's semantics, so a result can depend on the pair; the cases known are fixed by hints, listed under each source.

Rules on this page: 401, of which 252 are only the name of a rewrite function. A rule is printed as the translator runs it: the PostgreSQL pattern, its holes written `$name` (typed with `::type`), then the dialect's replacement.

The rows below are made on the Conformance (functions) legs of SingleStore: `singlestore` on none (the warehouse lane&#x27;s hosted SingleStore instance) (not judged by the last run). No run has verified them: run 45453337906, the last measured, judged none of its legs. Each row prints this provenance, read from scripts/conformance/function_legs.yaml and scripts/conformance/expected/functions.json, never written by hand.

275 of the grid's 629 features are native on SingleStore and left out.
